checks.summary: The three exact cross-route OPTIONS failures are source-evidenced and frozen to bounded rejection, absent permission headers, and zero manager or shutdown calls.
The packet defines an exact canonical policy for all three routes and explicitly forbids deriving allow values from caller input.
Unknown routes, missing required headers, and every extra header have stable allowed error outcomes with no permission, side effect, token, or stack disclosure.
The verified non-empty chunked shutdown gap maps directly to full decoded-body consumption and INVALID_BODY before any 202, callback, runtime removal, or listener close.
Both explicit zero length and empty chunked success paths are concrete, require end-of-stream validation, and preserve the existing 202 with exactly one delayed shutdown callback.
The owned tests can reproduce all four source failures and freeze the complete allow/deny matrix and framing cases without weakening existing assertions.
Full bridge and MCP regressions, scoped lint/build, mirror integrity, diff hygiene, and exact four-file ownership protect every passing source-task neighbor.
The command targets names owned by the two in-scope test files and will exercise only the route-specific preflight and shutdown-body regressions added by this remediation.
The existing command is real and fresh baseline execution passed all 5 current tests before remediation.
The existing task-scoped lint command covers every owned bridge file and fresh baseline execution exited 0.
The existing syntax build covers both production modules in scope and fresh baseline execution exited 0.
The existing MCP regression command is frozen to protect the imported renderer while MCP files remain outside remediation scope.
The exact mirror manifest command remains frozen while every mirror path is excluded from remediation scope.
Fresh preflight diff hygiene passed and the final check is bounded by the explicit four-file ownership rule.
The observable check copies the exact four source integration requests and requires rejection, no permission reflection, continued liveness, and zero side effects.
The matrix covers every valid route tuple, cross-route method, missing and extra header, case/order variant, and unknown route with canonical positive responses only.
The framing check covers zero, positive, absent, empty/non-empty chunked, slow, incomplete, aborted, and parser-rejected requests with callback timing and listener liveness assertions.
The check combines four-file diff review with all passing auth, Host, origin, capability, render, BUSY, redaction, cleanup, MCP, and mirror boundaries.
The remediation is limited to two bridge modules and two tests, changes no dependency or public feature surface, and is sequentially dependent on the source task.
The security-sensitive API change only narrows OPTIONS and shutdown acceptance and is covered by exact positive/negative matrices and unchanged error contracts.
Raw HTTP framing, Node parser behavior, route-specific CORS, listener continuity, and callback timing are directly observable without involving new external systems.
The remediation preserves token/body redaction, forbids permission reflection, adds no persistence, and asserts no runtime-state mutation on rejected shutdown requests.
